This authoring causes a publish-time crash in MAUI Blazor Hybrid apps that reference a Razor class library:\\n\\n```\\nerror : InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains more than one element\\n   at System.Linq.Enumerable.SingleOrDefault[TSource](IEnumerable`1 source)\\n   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.Tasks.GenerateStaticWebAssetEndpointsManifest.ComputeManifestAssets(...)\\n   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.Tasks.GenerateStaticWebAssetEndpointsManifest.Execute()\\n```\\n\\nThis is the root cause of **https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/54779** (and the .NET MAUI gallery regression https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/35953). The crash is in the SDK task, but the **fix belongs here**: the package should model `blazor.modules.json` as a **Framework static web asset**, the same way `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly` ships its framework assets. No SDK change is required.\\n\\n## Affected scenario\\n\\nA MAUI Blazor Hybrid app (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor`) that:\\n\\n1. References a Razor class library that contributes JS library modules (`*.lib.module.js`) and/or scoped CSS.\\n2. References `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView(.Maui)`, which contributes the fallback `_framework/blazor.modules.json`.\\n\\n`dotnet build` succeeds, but `dotnet publish` throws.\\n\\n## Root cause\\n\\nDuring **build**, the WebView package\\u0026#39;s `StaticWebAssets.Groups.targets`:\\n\\n- `_TagSdkModulesManifestWithGroup` promotes the SDK-generated JS modules manifest from `AssetKind=Build`/`AssetMode=CurrentProject` to `AssetKind=All`/`AssetMode=All`, tagging it `BlazorWebViewModules=default`.\\n- `_ResolveBlazorWebViewModulesGroup` resolves the **deferred** `BlazorWebViewModules` group based on `_ExistingBuildJSModules`, so the package fallback (`BlazorWebViewModules=fallback`) is excluded when the app generates its own manifest. Build works.\\n\\nDuring **publish**, group filtering runs with `SkipDeferred=\\u0026#34;true\\u0026#34;` (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Publish.targets`), so the deferred `BlazorWebViewModules` group is **not** resolved and the fallback is **not** excluded. The publish asset set for `_framework/blazor.modules.json` then contains:\\n\\n| Asset | SourceType | AssetKind | AssetGroups |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `blazor.modules.json` (package fallback) | Package | **All** | `BlazorWebViewModules=fallback` |\\n| `jsmodules.build.manifest.json` (promoted) | Computed | **All** | `BlazorWebViewModules=default` |\\n| `jsmodules.publish.manifest.json` | Computed | Publish | (empty) |\\n\\n`GenerateStaticWebAssetEndpointsManifest.ComputeManifestAssets` groups by target path and calls `ChooseNearestAssetKind(group, \\u0026#34;Publish\\u0026#34;).SingleOrDefault()`. With **two `All` assets**, `ChooseNearestAssetKind` yields both and `SingleOrDefault()` throws.\\n\\n## Proposed fix (idiomatic, in this repo)\\n\\nModel `blazor.modules.json` as a **Framework asset** instead of using the `BlazorWebViewModules` group + manifest-promotion machinery — exactly how `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly` ships its framework assets (`StaticWebAssetBasePath=/`, `StaticWebAssetFrameworkPattern=**/*.js`, no groups, no fallback/default variants — materialization alone handles it).\\n\\nConcretely, in `src/Components/WebView/WebView/src/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView.csproj`:\\n\\n```xml\\n\\n  \\n  /\\n  \\n  **/*.js;**/blazor.modules.json\\n\\n\\n\\n  \\n  \\n\\n```\\n\\nand **delete** `StaticWebAssets.Groups.targets` (the `BlazorWebViewModules` group definitions, `_TagSdkModulesManifestWithGroup`, and `_ResolveBlazorWebViewModulesGroup`). Keep the `JSModuleManifestRelativePath=_framework/blazor.modules.json` and `CompressionEnabled=false` properties in the package\\u0026#39;s build props.\\n\\n### Why this works\\n\\nThe framework asset is **materialized once into the consuming project at build** (`SourceType` → `Discovered`, `AssetMode=CurrentProject`, materialized under `obj/.../fx/`). From then on it is an ordinary project asset that flows through publish without re-introducing a cross-project `Package` asset.\\n\\n- **App has its own JS modules:** the materialized fallback is `All`; the app\\u0026#39;s generated manifest is `Build`/`Publish`. At publish there is a single `All` plus the `Publish` asset on the route, so `ChooseNearestAssetKind` picks the `Publish` asset cleanly — **no two-`All` collision, no crash**. The app\\u0026#39;s manifest wins.\\n- **App has no JS modules:** no manifest is generated, so the materialized fallback at `_framework/blazor.modules.json` is the one that is served — the fallback still works.\\n\\nTwo important details:\\n\\n1. Use `StaticWebAssetBasePath=/` with `_framework/` **in the relative path** (i.e. ship the file at `wwwroot/_framework/blazor.modules.json`). With `BasePath=/_framework` and a root-level relative path, materialization rebases to the consumer\\u0026#39;s `BasePath` (`/`) and the asset lands at `blazor.modules.json` instead of `_framework/blazor.modules.json`. `Components.WebAssembly` already follows the `BasePath=/` + `_framework/`-in-relative-path convention.\\n2. The `**/blazor.modules.json` framework pattern is matched against the relative path **without fingerprint tokens**; this works regardless of fingerprinting.\\n\\n## Repro / validation\\n\\nI reproduced the crash and validated the fix with a self-contained integration test in dotnet/sdk (no SDK code change), using a packed package that simulates the WebView package and a Razor class library:\\n\\n- Group authoring (current) → `dotnet publish` fails with `Sequence contains more than one element`.\\n- `blazor.modules.json` modeled as a Framework asset → `dotnet publish` succeeds with a single `_framework/blazor.modules.json` (the app\\u0026#39;s generated manifest), and the fallback-only case (no app modules) is served by the materialized package manifest.\\n\\n(The test lives in `test/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tests/MauiBlazorHybridWebViewIntegrationTest.cs` + `test/TestAssets/TestProjects/MauiBlazorHybridWebView` in dotnet/sdk and can serve as a reference for the expected behavior.)\\n\\n## Related\\n\\n- dotnet/sdk#54779 — the `Sequence contains more than one element` crash (root cause analysis above).\\n- dotnet/maui#35953 — the MAUI gallery regression; Disposing an `IJSObjectReference` after the WebView had gone threw `JSDisconnectedException`, which showed up as hangs on teardown and alarming errors in the debug output. Navigation and disposal now mark the JS runtime disconnected before components are disposed, and that exception is caught and discarded.\\n\\nThis validates that a Hybrid app tears down cleanly.\\n\\n## Minimum build\\n\\n.NET 11 Preview 7 or later.\\n\\n## Configurations to cover\\n\\n* Blazor Web App\\n  * [ ] Static SSR\\n  * [ ] Interactive Server\\n  * [ ] Interactive WebAssembly\\n  * [ ] Interactive Auto\\n* [ ] Standalone WebAssembly\\n* [x] Hybrid (MAUI)\\n\\n## Also exercise\\n\\n* [ ] Published output\\n* [ ] An existing .NET 10 app upgraded to .NET 11\\n* [ ] Trimming or ahead-of-time compilation\\n* [ ] More than one server instance, or a proxy in front\\n* [ ] Hot Reload\\n* [ ] An IDE as well as the command line\\n* [ ] Container\\n\\n## Setup\\n\\nYou need the workloads for building a native app for at least one platform, and a device or emulator. Covering more than one platform is worthwhile, since the embedded browser differs between them.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nA native app hosting Blazor, with pages that are busy in ways that make teardown awkward. Include a page that keeps a JavaScript module loaded and calls into it repeatedly, one that starts a slow JavaScript call and does not wait for it, one with a timer that keeps firing, and one that has registered .NET methods for JavaScript to call back into. Give the components proper cleanup so you can tell whether it runs. Add a native page alongside the Blazor content so you can move between the two kinds of screen, and log to the debug output when each component is cleaned up.\\n\\n## Things to try\\n\\n* Navigating away from each busy page while it is mid-flight.\\n* Moving from a Blazor screen to a native screen and back, repeatedly.\\n* Closing the app while a page is in the middle of a JavaScript call.\\n* Backgrounding the app and returning to it, and backgrounding it and then closing it.\\n* Using the operating system\\u0026#39;s back gesture or button rather than in-app navigation.\\n* Rotating the device while a page is busy.\\n* Repeating the cycle many times in one session and watching memory.\\n* Watching the debug output throughout for exceptions and warnings.\\n\\n## Expected behavior\\n\\nTeardown completes promptly however busy the page was, and calls that were already in flight go quietly.\\n\\n### Must hold\\n\\n* Leaving each busy page runs its cleanup and does not hang.\\n* Closing the app while a JavaScript call is in flight terminates promptly rather than waiting on work that will never finish.\\n* No exception from calls that were in flight appears in the debug output. The `blazorwebworker` template scaffolds a client that moves that work onto a web worker so the page stays responsive. This validates that the template produces a working project, that the generated client offloads work as intended, and that the app stays usable while the worker is busy.\\n\\n**It also validates that a reported bug is fixed.** A worker that ran correctly during development failed in the **published** app with `Unhandled exception rendering component: Worker encountered an error` in the browser console, because the worker could not resolve the fingerprinted framework files. Publishing is therefore not an optional extra here; it is where the bug lived. ([#65820](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65820))\\n\\n## Minimum build\\n\\n.NET 11 Preview 7 or later.\\n\\n## Configurations to cover\\n\\n* Blazor Web App\\n  * [ ] Static SSR\\n  * [ ] Interactive Server\\n  * [x] Interactive WebAssembly\\n  * [ ] Interactive Auto\\n* [x] Standalone WebAssembly\\n* [ ] Hybrid (MAUI)\\n\\nWeb workers only exist in the browser, so the worker is reachable only from client-side rendered code. Interactive Server and static SSR are out of scope.\\n\\n## Also exercise\\n\\n* [x] Published output\\n* [ ] An existing .NET 10 app upgraded to .NET 11\\n* [x] Trimming or ahead-of-time compilation\\n* [ ] More than one server instance, or a proxy in front\\n* [ ] Hot Reload\\n* [x] An IDE as well as the command line\\n* [ ] Container\\n\\n## Setup\\n\\nCreate the worker project with `dotnet new blazorwebworker`, and also from the template list in an IDE, since the rename from the old .NET Web Worker name is part of what is being validated. Reference it from a Blazor app that renders on the client.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nA Blazor app with a page that gives the user something to do while work is happening: a counter they can click, an input they can type into, or an animation. Reference a project created from the `blazorwebworker` template.\\n\\nIn the worker project, add `[JSExport]` methods next to the generated `Greet` sample: one that returns a value after several seconds of real computation, one that returns nothing, and one that throws. Then call them from the page through `WebWorkerClient`, using `InvokeAsync` for the first and `InvokeVoidAsync` for the second, and show the results on screen.\\n\\nAdd the same slow computation on the main thread as well, behind its own button, so you have a direct comparison.\\n\\n## Things to try\\n\\n* Running the slow work on the main thread and then in the worker, clicking the counter throughout both.\\n* **Publishing the app and running the published output.** This is the reported repro: the worker worked in development and failed once published, where framework files are fingerprinted. Do this early rather than last.\\n* Calling the method that returns nothing and confirming it ran.\\n* Calling the method that throws, and reading what reaches the .NET side.\\n* Several calls in flight at once.\\n* Disposing the client while a call is still running, and navigating away mid-call.\\n* Creating a second client on the same page.\\n* Publishing with trimming or ahead-of-time compilation enabled.\\n* Creating the project from the IDE template list as well as from the command line.\\n\\n## Expected behavior\\n\\nWork handed to the worker runs off the main thread, and the page stays usable while it does.\\n\\n### Must hold\\n\\n* `dotnet new blazorwebworker` creates a project that builds without edits, and the template is listed under that name in `dotnet new list` and in the IDE.\\n* While the worker is running the slow computation, the counter still increments and the page still repaints. Running the same computation on the main thread visibly blocks it.\\n* `InvokeAsync` returns the worker\\u0026#39;s value, and `InvokeVoidAsync` runs the method and completes without asking for one.\\n* An exception thrown inside the worker surfaces on the .NET side as a failure carrying a usable message, rather than hanging or failing silently.\\n* Disposing the client, and navigating away mid-call, produce no unhandled error in the browser console.\\n* The published app loads its worker successfully, with no failed request for framework files in the network log, and no `Worker encountered an error` message in the browser console.\\n\\n### Expected differences between configurations\\n\\n* No differences are expected between Standalone WebAssembly and a Blazor Web App\\u0026#39;s Interactive WebAssembly pages.\\n\\n## Evidence to capture\\n\\nA short screen recording showing the counter continuing to respond while the worker runs the slow computation, and the same counter freezing when the computation runs on the main thread.\\n\\n## Documentation to use\\n\\n* [New Blazor Web Worker template, .NET 11 release notes](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-11#new-blazor-web-worker-template-blazorwebworker)\\n* [ASP.NET Core Blazor with .NET on web workers](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/blazor/blazor-with-dotnet-on-web-workers?view=aspnetcore-11.0)\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nReport results using the format described in the [validation testing manual](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68479). Include link to a repository with the test app.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68818\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"oroztocil\",\"id\":79744616,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/oroztocil\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/79744616?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Validation\",\"validation-scenario\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-rc2\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-26T15:24:22Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T15:25:22Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

I did not want to deal with hosting them on separate paths (through things like `` as it involved an existing application which would have been difficult to migrate, so they are exposed on separate domains. \\n\\nTo separate their assets I have been using \\u0026#34;StaticWebAssetBasePath\\u0026#34; in the csproj\\u0026#39;s to g et two folders in the wwwroot (say app-1 and app-2). So for the sake of discussion, i have app.com which gets (largely) served from wwwroot/app-1 and my.app.com which gets (largely) served from wwwroot/app-2. They are both able to use the same api which is accessible by route /api/xxx.\\n\\nSome issues I had with this are that the server had to be modified slightly to point the applications to the correct paths for certain requests (mostly different PathBase)\\n- the `_content` directory is  published in the wwwroot instead of wwwroot/app-1, requests to assets here seem to work with the PathBase changes on the server.\\n- resourcecollection.{fingerprint}.js and blazor.web.js do not exist on disk but generated by some middleware, it wont be served correctly unless the request pipeline has the correct PathBase set (app-1/app-2).\\n- _framework/dotnet.js will not be found with these PathBase changes on the server. I have to manually prepend the PathBase _again_ to find the file like `/app-1/app-1/_framework/dotnet.js`. \\n\\nSo at this point I hack in a little middleware that essentially checks for any path `some.file` if `{pathbase}/some.file` exists on disk. Note that this does mean we are already looking for `app-1/_framework/dotnet.js` so we add the \\u0026#34;missing\\u0026#34; segment.\\n\\nNow here we are, up and running. A bit wacky that is has to be like this but sure. However, I noticed that fingerprinting is now suffering from the same weird double PathBase requirement issue:\\n- Like with _framework/dotnet.js, I am already effectively serving `/app-1/app-1/main.js`. Even though the browser thinks its serving `/main.js`. To reiterate, I have to .UsePathBase in program.cs AND the middleware that adds the pathbase again, to the actual request path.\\n- The fingerprinded asset paths (resolved in App.razor through the ComponentBase.Assets property) do not work either unless the path base is included in the path `/app-1/main.js`. \\n\\nIn the last point, I would be adding the pathbase THREE times. Amazingly, this would in turn break the resolution of _framework.dotnet.js and my middleware hack (which I am not keen on keeping) cannot work around this by checking for a file on disk, because only the StaticAssetsEndpointDataSource which knows which file the path may map to.\\n\\nSo I have gotten a bit stuck here. \\n\\n\\n\\n\\n  \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\n1. Static asset requests involving assets in a StaticAssetsBasePath directory need not add multiple PathBase\\u0026#39;s in the request uri to be resolved, wether they are fingerprinted or not. \\n2. Fingerprinting url resolution considers the StaticAssetsBasePath\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nSample blazor web repo + add an extra client.\\n\\nServe each client from a separate \\u0026#39;sub application\\u0026#39; using `MapWhen(ctx =\\u0026gt; domain == x, app =\\u0026gt; configureApp(app)`. and configure each app with a separate PathBase and UseEndpoints with MapStaticAssets and MapRazorComponents/MapRazorPages.\\n\\nThen set the StaticAssetsBasePath in each blazor client\\u0026#39;s csproj file, matching the respective pathbases ofcourse.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n9.0.203\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/62249\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"ArcadeMode\",\"id\":5969155,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/ArcadeMode\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/5969155?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"investigate\",\"area-blazor\"],\"assignees\":[\"javiercn\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-06-04T19:19:54Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-01-25T10:07:44Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

No runtime code inspects or rewrites values.\\n\\n## Motivation and goals\\n\\nBlazor applications currently write explicit expressions such as `@Assets[\\u0026#34;images/logo.png\\u0026#34;]` to resolve fingerprinted static web assets. Common HTML scenarios become repetitive, while automatically treating arbitrary component parameters as asset paths would create silent false positives.\\n\\nThe proposal aims to:\\n\\n- Keep common static asset references concise without adding Razor syntax.\\n- Require explicit component parameter opt-in.\\n- Define a conservative built-in HTML allowlist.\\n- Give component libraries a discoverable opt-in contract.\\n- Preserve existing behavior for nonqualifying values and locations.\\n- Provide a default-on, per-project MSBuild opt-out.\\n\\n## In scope\\n\\n- A public `[AssetPath]` marker for individual string component parameters.\\n- Public `[AcceptsAssetPath(elementName, attributeName)]` metadata for HTML element/attribute pairs.\\n- Razor compile-time expansion of complete static literals beginning exactly with `~/`.\\n- Initial built-in HTML support for `img[src]`, `link[href]`, and `script[src]`.\\n- `RazorEnableAssetPathExpansion`, enabled by default and independently configurable for each application or Razor class library.\\n- Declaration diagnostics for `[AssetPath]` used without `[Parameter]` or on a non-string property.\\n- An audit of built-in Blazor component APIs.\\n\\n## Out of scope\\n\\n- Inferring asset semantics from names such as `Source`, `Src`, `Href`, or `Url`.\\n- Runtime string inspection, runtime registration, middleware, services, or render-tree rewriting.\\n- C# expressions, interpolated values, attribute splatting, CSS, JavaScript, `style`, or `srcset` parsing.\\n- Navigation and submission locations such as `a[href]` and `form[action]`.\\n- Changes to static web asset discovery, fingerprint generation, publication, or lookup fallback.\\n- Adding new string URL parameters to existing built-in components as part of this feature.\\n\\n## Risks / unknowns\\n\\n- Delivery requires coordinated changes in `dotnet/aspnetcore`, `dotnet/roslyn`, and `dotnet/sdk`.\\n- The Razor team must confirm the metadata descriptor mechanism for data consumed by a lowering pass without ordinary tag matching.\\n- The exact Razor language-version gate and package-flow order need agreement.\\n- Custom Razor base classes without a compatible `Assets` member would receive a C# compile error when using the concise syntax.\\n- Supported IDE hosts must be validated for compiler-visible MSBuild property propagation.\\n- API review must confirm names and whether third-party HTML-pair extension remains open.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\nBuilt-in HTML:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\u003cimg src=\\\"~/images/logo.png\\\" alt=\\\"Company logo\\\"/\\u003e\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\nThe Razor compiler generates behavior equivalent to:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\u003cimg src=\\\"@Assets[\\\" alt=\\\"Company logo\\\"/\\u003e\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\nComponent opt-in:\\n\\n```csharp\\npublic class Image : ComponentBase\\n{\\n    [Parameter]\\n    [AssetPath]\\n    public string? Source { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```razor\\n\\n```\\n\\nThe component receives the same value as:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\n```\\n\\nPer-project opt-out:\\n\\n```xml\\n\\n  false\\n\\n```\\n\\nWhen disabled, Razor leaves `~/` literals unchanged in that project\\u0026#39;s Razor files. When using `.UseStaticFiles()`, the new `.AddInteractiveServerComponents()` and the old `.MapBlazorHub()` no longer result in those files being served. This is what #64381 reports.\\n\\n## Motivation and goals\\n\\nThis removes the unnecessary overhead of being forced to migrate to `.MapStaticAssets()` when migrating to .NET 10. It also solves the significant headache of discovering that this is the solution to an obscure error in the first place. For example, I personally had to do a lot of research to understand how this would impact my custom Webpack pipeline.\\n\\n## In scope\\n\\n- #64381\\n  - This is the exact motivating issue.\\n\\n## Out of scope\\n\\n- #57756\\n  - `.UseBlazorFrameworkFiles()` and `.MapBlazorHub()` are wrapped by the newer `.AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents()` and `.AddInteractiveServerComponents()` respectively, both of which are designed to play nice with `.MapStaticAssets()`. This could be solved by the methods performing the same check and throwing an exception if static assets are mapped. Not relevant to this though.\\n\\n## Risks / unknowns\\n\\nThis restores half-deleted functionality (only the server side) and without clear guidance as to how to adapt without having to search through GitHub issues. I don\\u0026#39;t believe this is a risk or blocker for future features.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\nIn the following examples, `.MapStaticAssets()` is NOT called, and it\\u0026#39;s assumed that `.UseRouting()` is called before `.UseStaticFiles()` so that the static files middleware is endpoint-aware. The following no longer works in .NET 10:\\n\\n```cs\\napp.UseStaticFiles();\\napp.MapRazorComponents().AddInteractiveServerComponents();\\n```\\n\\n```cs\\napp.UseStaticFiles();\\napp.MapBlazorHub();\\n```\\n\\nBut these still do:\\n\\n```cs\\napp.UseStaticFiles();\\napp.MapRazorComponents().AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents();\\n```\\n\\n```cs\\napp.UseStaticFiles();\\napp.UseBlazorFrameworkFiles();\\n```\\n\\nBoth should work.\\n\\n# Research\\n\\nThis issue appears to be a mistake, not an intentional change. Here\\u0026#39;s the timeline I discovered:\\n\\n1. The static asset guard is introduced to only the wasm endpoints. It is never added to the server endpoints. See: #55558\\n2. The static asset guard is changed from `if (wasmWithOptions is { EndpointOptions.ConventionsApplied: true })` to `if (applicationBuilder.Properties[ResourceCollectionKey] is ResourceAssetCollection assetMap)`. See: #56045\\n3. At some point, the unified endpoint `blazor.web.js` is added into the mix. See: #47605\\n4. #58721 implements the switch to serving `blazor.*.js` files as static assets. In the same batch of changes, however, the server endpoints are just dropped entirely. Presumably this made sense without the context of this papertrail.\\n\\n# Detailed design\\n\\nGiven the evidence, I believe the correct (and very simple) fix is to re-add the server and unified endpoints (`blazor.server.js` and `blazor.web.js`), but under the same guard as the wasm endpoints. This was likely the correct course of action to begin with when looking at the big picture.\\n\\n## Key decisions\\n\\n- Since the old versions of the endpoints read from embedded resources, the new versions will instead mimic how the wasm endpoints are read from static files.\\n- The old versions returned the map files for the `blazor.*.js` files guarded by `#if DEBUG` for internal testing purposes. Given that they were removed and probably are configured to exist as static assets for internal testing, these will not be added back.\\n- The wasm endpoints have very elaborate static files options, whereas the server and unified endpoints had very basic ones. In Blazor we use the .NET trimmer to significantly reduce the publish size of Blazor WebAssembly apps. However, we don\\u0026#39;t currently use the .NET trimmer to its fullest potential. We currently configure the trimmer in a partial mode, which only trims assemblies that are explicitly marked as trimmable. This typically means that the app assembly itself and many dependencies are not trimmed. This is a conservative setting that optimizes for maintaining functionality over reducing app size. \\n\\nThe default trim mode for the .NET trimmer is to trim everything. This is the mode used by the .NET Native AOT workloads.Analyzers provide warnings if there are code paths in the app that are not safe to trim. Given how sensitive web apps are to download size and load time, it seems like doing full trimming should be the goal for Blazor.\\n\\nEnabling support for full trimming also is a potential solution to enabling a [single project model for Blazor Web Apps](#49079) that target both server and browser. When you multitarget a project, everything in the project is built for both targets unless you indicated otherwise. This is problematic for browser scenarios because you may potentially bring in dependencies, components, and code into the browser targeted build that are only needed on the server. However, if we could enable full trimming *and* indicate to the trimmer which components are setup to render on WebAssembly, then the browser build could be aggressively trimmed to remove any unwanted code and dependencies.\\n\\nEnabling support for full .NET trimming typically means removing any dynamic code path that are based on reflection. We would need to make Blazor apps trimmer friendly by removing this code using techniques like source generators. For example, in Blazor we use reflection as part of the component discovery process and in the render tree builder code generated by the Razor compiler. We\\u0026#39;re already working on enabling [component discovery through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48767). We also have on our backlog to [handle component parameters through source generation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/29550). There may be other related work items as well.\\n\\nThere is also ecosystem impact of enabling full trimming by default. Many .NET libraries are not setup for trimming and would potentially need to be updated. It will take some time to work through these issues with the Blazor community. Certain features also simply wouldn\\u0026#39;t work with full trimming. For example, dynamically loading dependencies at runtime that are not known statically. For backwards compatibility, app developers can configure the trimmer to not trim assemblies that are not yet trimmer friendly. We\\u0026#39;d need to understand better all the cases that get impacted by full trimming and ensure we provide a reasonable user experience for addressing them.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49409\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"danroth27\",\"id\":1874516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/danroth27\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1874516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"Priority:1\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\",\"feature-trimming\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":20,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":46,\"+1\":43,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":3},\"created_at\":\"2023-07-14T14:49:12Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-12-06T11:52:00Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T20:42:23.447Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7092b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":58811,\"title\":\"[Blazor] Improving ASP.NET Core integration\",\"body\":\"There are certain design choices in components that Blazor ships out of the box that make it hard to write applications that can work seamlessly on SSR scenarios and on interactive modes. This causes friction as there are many cases where the behavior is different on SSR and on Interactive sessions and developers have to account for both cases. Below is a non-exhaustive list of improvements that we can do to improve some of these experiences:\\n* Routing:\\n  * There are two routers, one on the server (ASP.NET Core) and one on the client. We\\u0026#39;ve merged the two implementations for the most part, but there are details that still cause confusion.\\n   * The need to declare additional assemblies in two locations: We should make the endpoint in ASP.NET Core pass along the configured assemblies to the client project via persisted state or some other mechanism.\\n   * Differences in handling `NotFound`: On SSR scenarios this is represented by an endpoint, on the interactive router with a `RenderFragment`. We should extend the router to take in a `NotFoundPage` parameter that can be used during SSR and Interactive rendering to display not found content.\\n   * Lack of `NavigationManager.NotFound()` or equivalent API for triggering `NotFound` on Blazor applications. This would trigger a 404 response on SSR scenarios that would render the `NotFound` page/component and on InteractiveScenarios it would signal any registered callback (the router) the equivalent situation (which would trigger the render).\\n   * Similar deal for triggering errors through an `Error` page.\\n * Authentication:\\n   * In ASP.NET Core you can use `Challenge` to trigger/start the authentication process. There is no Blazor equivalent for it, so users end up having to manually redirect users on interactive sessions.\\n   * We should extend `AuthenticationStateProvider` or similar APIs to support this type of scenario. On interactive sessions, a `Challenge` for a scheme will always result in a redirect (maybe challenge is not the right way to call this, and we should be using `RedirectToLogin` or some other verb. For server scenarios the information about the configured schemes is already available. For `WebAssembly` scenarios, information about the redirect URL can be provided via some mechanism like PersistedState. For schemes that need to generate additional information (like nonces, etc.) they\\u0026#39;ll be extended to add at least a new endpoint (maybe two) to handle the bootstrapping of the authentication process so that interactive clients (like webassembly) can redirect to a well-known URL to start the process.\\n* Lazy loading:\\n  * With prerendering, it can happen that we prerender a path that requires lazy loaded assemblies to render. The current APIs don\\u0026#39;t offer a way to make sure those assemblies are loaded before the page tries to render, which results in failures when the app goes interactive. We need:\\n  * A `LazyAssemblyLoader` implementation for prerendering (if you try to do this on any current .NET version it will fail).\\n  * For a given page, a list of all the dependent assemblies that are lazy loaded.\\n    * The ability to determine if they need to be immediately loaded for the page to render (for example, if the page references a type `B` that lives on a lazy loaded assembly on its `type definition` (`class A { public B BProp { get; set; } })` or if it can be delayed (because B is only used inside a method body).\\n  * A way to tell the runtime to load those assemblies when booting webassembly as we know they\\u0026#39;ll be needed immediately.\\n* Built-in components:\\n  * In general, we need to look at every component that we ship and ensure there\\u0026#39;s a way for them to work on each render mode in a reasonable way across render modes.\\n  * QuickGrid.\\n  * NavLink.\\n  * EditForm.\\n  * Section(s)\\n  * Cascading parameters.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/58811\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Pillar: Dev Experience\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":5,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":5},\"created_at\":\"2024-11-06T09:38:38Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:05:35Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":true,\"sub_issues_summary\":{\"total\":7,\"completed\":4,\"percent_completed\":57},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Please describe the problem.\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m trying to calculate SRI hashes for the static web assets in my Blazor Web App.\\nAt the moment, the suggested way for static data is simply to calculate it elsewhere and paste the SRI hash into my App..razor.\\nSee https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/security/content-security-policy?view=aspnetcore-9.0#adopt-subresource-integrity-sri\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;d like an built-in way to do that\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\nSomething like a new method in  ComponentBase, similar to ``Assets``, called ``AssetIntegrity``\\n```csharp\\n\\n```\\n\\n\\n### Additional context\\n\\nI looked at the build-time staticwebassets.build.json, there is already a property called Integrity, which is used for ETag and (I think) for ``ImportMap``. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/fundamentals/static-files?view=aspnetcore-9.0#import-maps \\n\\nI looked at runtime into the data structures behind ``Assets``, ``ResourceAssetCollection``, but I couldn\\u0026#39;t find the ``Integrity``  property anywhere.\\n\\n\\nThere is some prior discussins about CSP in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/6001, but that includes a fully features CSP builder.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/61180\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Tornhoof\",\"id\":7989549,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Tornhoof\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/7989549?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"CONTRIBUTOR\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-03-27T07:00:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-05-01T13:11:52Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Users have to make a choice between:\\n* Per page interactivity vs Global interactivity\\n* SSR, Server, WebAssembly or a combination thereof.\\n* Auth options\\n\\nThis can be challenging (specially the render modes and per page vs global interactivity) and might not be optimal for newcomers to the framework.\\n\\nWhile we want to retain all these options in the template, however, it might be good if we can create \\u0026#34;blessed paths\\u0026#34; within the template/UI to some of the most popular combinations (Global interactivity + Wasm + Prerendering (Hosted wasm)) and (Global interactivity + Server + No-Prerendering) + auth options.\\n\\nAn alternative might be a different experience that provides more information inline to make a decision or a \\u0026#34;quickstart\\u0026#34; template that doesn\\u0026#39;t give you options (or only gives you server/client) so that you can get started quickly and leave the existing template as it is.\\n\\nAnother alternative is to remove all the options (except for the most basic ones) from the template and use scaffolders to bring in functionality as needed.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/60311\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":5,\"+1\":3,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":2,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-02-11T12:51:14Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-02-11T13:07:17Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}
